parallel.requirements: Recognized the Python script as argparse with required --a and boltons.strutils.slugify, plus ESM .mjs, local imports only, manual argv parsing, and output under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The root kept final ownership while delegating CLI probing and slugify probing; children also implemented pieces or whole alternates, with the root choosing and patching the delivered /output tree.
parallel.implementation: Produced /output/test4.mjs with local app, CLI, and slugify modules; it handled help, required --a, repeated flags, empty values, some negative-number handling, separators, Unicode, emoji, and backslash preservation from probes.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The root inspected both /output and /workspace/output trees, used the required /output tree, incorporated the child backslash finding, and delivered the /output module hierarchy.
parallel.verification: Ran side-by-side checks against the executable on help/error cases, repeated --a, empty values, help prefixes, negative numbers, -- handling, Unicode, emoji, euro sign, and backslashes.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite sampled parity checks and a valid artifact, the official evaluator completed with 49/166 and solution_passed false, indicating hidden behavioral gaps shared with the serial run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same ESM .mjs, manual argv, no-dependency, /output delivery requirements and the actual --a CLI option from the executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the entire workflow: locate source and executable, probe black-box behavior, write modules, patch mismatches, verify, and finalize.
serial.implementation: Produced /output/test4.mjs with CLI and slugify modules; it patched separator-only output, underscore separator handling, and -- sentinel behavior after comparison failures.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All files were written under /output with local .mjs imports, and the final response listed the resulting module hierarchy and entry file.
serial.verification: Ran comparison harnesses against the executable on success, help, error, negative-number, --, Unicode, punctuation, and backslash cases, then reported sampled parity except expected program-name differences.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also completed with 49/166 and solution_passed false, so hidden coverage exceeded the sampled probes without a parallel-specific explanation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same explicit task requirements: ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, local imports only, and output in /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and the actual --a option from the executable rather than using the prompt example --arg literally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both built around the same required option and ESM/no-dependency constraints.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across a root, a CLI probe child, a slugify probe child, and a nested slugify probe, while the root retained final closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept probing, implementation, patching, and verification in one actor with no child-agent delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced redundant and overlapping probes; serial was linear, but both reached an owned implementation and final response.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child reports surfaced CLI and slugify findings, including a backslash exception, and the parent consumed them before patching.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried its own probe results forward directly into parser and slugifier patches without handoff boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel run had handoff boundaries, but the important received information was used rather than lost or left conflicting.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a modular /output implementation, then patched parser prefix handling and slugify separator behavior after probes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a modular /output implementation and patched slugify and parser mismatches found by its own harness.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete code paths differed in module names and ownership, but both converged on similar sampled behavior and the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel waited for children, timed out once, later received slugify and CLI final answers, and proceeded after inspection.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child lifecycle to manage; results were local probe outputs and final local verification results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had extra lifecycle activity, but no completed result was visibly trapped or ignored before final delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had both /output and /workspace/output trees present, then inspected them and delivered the required /output artifact tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote only the required /output tree for delivery and listed those artifacts in the final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an extra alternate implementation tree, but there is no evidence it contaminated or replaced the delivered /output tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran normalized side-by-side tests after code patches and reported passing sampled checks before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a comparison harness, found mismatches, patched them, and reran until sampled checks matched.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both relied on sampled black-box checks and both missed hidden evaluator behavior, producing identical failed official outcomes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent more time and tokens with four covered rollouts and several child interactions, but still closed normally without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one rollout, fewer requests and tokens, and also closed normally without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was costlier and more redundant, yet this did not create a distinct adverse closure effect; official scores were identical.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation is not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 49 of 166 passing samples. The task-solving difference is process shape, not final quality: parallel used child probes and an alternate /workspace/output tree, while serial stayed single-agent, but both delivered modular ESM implementations under /output and both relied on sampled parity checks that did not cover enough hidden evaluator cases.
parallel_contributors: Used child probes to broaden CLI and slugify exploration, then incorporated the backslash finding and patched /output before final checks.
serial_contributors: Used a single linear probing and patching loop that found similar separator, underscore, and -- sentinel issues before final checks.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both failures are best explained as ordinary incomplete black-box emulation against hidden evaluator cases, not by a realized parallel coordination error.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator used 166 samples; both attempts passed only 49 despite reporting sampled local parity.
